Oxygen exists as simple O₂ molecules with relatively few electrons and small molecular size, resulting in weak London dispersion forces. In contrast, sulfur forms larger S₈ ring structures with more electrons and greater surface area for intermolecular attractions, leading to stronger forces between molecules and thus a higher melting point..
